BEGIN RID PROTOCOL  

STEP 1 — PRE-COMMITMENT  

Causal-identification strategy  
• Treatment = inclusion on Fortune’s “100 Best Companies to Work For” list (publicly announced each January).  
• Counterfactual = publicly listed firms not on the list, matched on industry, size and book-to-market, or standard risk factors.  
• Identification relies on the listing date as an exogenous, publicly observed shock to investor information about employee satisfaction. Risk-adjusted abnormal returns after the listing date identify any under-pricing of this intangible asset.  

Directional hypothesis (cannot be changed later)  
H1: Firms included on the list earn POSITIVE abnormal stock returns (alpha > 0) in the 12 months following publication, after controlling for Fama-French-Carhart factors and standard firm characteristics.  

STEP 2 — SPECIFICATION DISCIPLINE  
Exactly five specifications will be estimated; no others.

Spec 1 – Equal-weighted calendar-time portfolio regression  
rt = α + βMKT · MKTt + βSMB · SMBt + βHML · HMLt + βUMD · UMDt + εt  
rt = monthly excess return on an equal-weighted portfolio of all list firms, held from month 1 to 12 after each annual announcement. Sample: Feb 1984 – Jan 2010 (312 months).

Spec 2 – Value-weighted calendar-time portfolio regression  
Identical to Spec 1 but with value-weighted returns.

Spec 3 – Firm-level panel with POST indicator  
(Ri,t – Rf,t) = α + β factors + γ POSTi,t + δ Xi,t-1 + μi + τt + εi,t  
POSTi,t = 1 for months 1-12 after a firm appears on the list, 0 otherwise. Xi,t-1 = log(size), log(book-to-market), past 12-month return. Firm and year fixed effects; errors clustered by firm.

Spec 4 – Matched difference-in-differences on 12-month CAR  
CARi = θ Treatedi + φ Controls + εi  
Treated = 1 if on list. Controls: same as Xi. Matching: nearest-neighbor within industry-year on size & B/M. Outcome = cumulative abnormal return (factor alpha summed) months 1-12.

Spec 5 – Event-study dynamic leads/lags around first inclusion  
Estimate γk in: (Ri,t – Rf,t) = Σk≠-1 γk DKi,t + β factors + μi + τt + εi,t  
k = -24…+24 monthly bins; DK=1 if month t is k relative to first inclusion (-1 omitted). Test joint insignificance of leads k = -24…-1. Graph not required; coefficients stored.

STEP 3 — FALSIFICATION GATE  

The directional hypothesis H1 will be rejected if ANY of the following hold:  
FG-1: In BOTH Spec 1 and Spec 2, α ≤ 0 OR |t| < 1.64 (p > 0.10, two-sided).  
FG-2: In Spec 3, γ ≤ 0 OR p > 0.10.  
FG-3: In Spec 5, a Wald test shows the 24 pre-treatment γk jointly differ from zero at p < 0.10 (pre-trend violation).  
FG-4: Calendar-time regression Newey-West (12 lags) α-t statistics < 1.64 (robustness failure).  

If any gate trips, we deem H1 falsified.

STEP 4 — R CODE (self-contained, only the 5 specs)

```r
############################################################
# Required packages
############################################################
libs <- c("tidyverse","fixest","MatchIt","lmtest","sandwich")
invisible(lapply(libs, require, character.only = TRUE))

############################################################
# 0.  LOAD DATA  (user must supply)
############################################################
# Assumed objects:
# fortune      : data.frame(firm_id, list_year, ann_date)            # January announcement date
# crsp_monthly : data.frame(firm_id, date, ret, me, prc)             # monthly CRSP (ret in decimal)
# factors      : data.frame(date, MKT, SMB, HML, UMD, RF)            # FF-Carhart + risk-free
# compustat    : data.frame(firm_id, fyear, size=at, bm=bm)          # annual accounting

############################################################
# 1.  PREP DATA
############################################################
# Merge monthly returns with factors
ret <- crsp_monthly %>%
  left_join(factors, by = "date") %>%
  mutate(excess = ret - RF)

# Build POST indicator (months 1-12 after each annual list)
post_frame <- fortune %>%
  select(firm_id, ann_date) %>%
  mutate(start = ann_date %m+% months(1),
         end   = ann_date %m+% months(12))

# Expand to monthly sequence
post_months <- post_frame %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  do(data.frame(firm_id = .$firm_id,
                date    = seq(.$start, .$end, by = "month"))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(POST = 1)

# Firm-level panel
panel <- ret %>%
  left_join(post_months, by = c("firm_id","date")) %>%
  mutate(POST = replace_na(POST,0))

# Add lagged controls
controls <- compustat %>%
  mutate(fyear_end = ymd(paste0(fyear,"-12-31"))) %>%
  select(firm_id, fyear_end, size, bm)

panel <- panel %>%
  left_join(controls, by = c("firm_id" = "firm_id",
                             "date" = "fyear_end")) %>%
  group_by(firm_id) %>%
  fill(size, bm, .direction = "down") %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(lsize = log(size),
         lbm   = log(bm),
         mom12 = lag(rollapply(ret, 12, FUN = function(x) prod(1+x)-1, fill = NA),1))

############################################################
# 2.  SPEC 1 & 2 : CALENDAR-TIME PORTFOLIOS
############################################################
# Build rebalanced portfolios (equal and value weighted)
port <- panel %>%
  filter(POST==1) %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarise(eq_ret  = mean(ret, na.rm=TRUE),
            vw_ret  = weighted.mean(ret, w = me, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  left_join(factors, by="date") %>%
  mutate(eq_excess = eq_ret - RF,
         vw_excess = vw_ret - RF)

# Spec 1: equal-weighted
spec1 <- lm(eq_excess ~ MKT + SMB + HML + UMD, data=port)
coeftest(spec1, vcov = NeweyWest(spec1, lag = 12, prewhite = FALSE))

# Spec 2: value-weighted
spec2 <- lm(vw_excess ~ MKT + SMB + HML + UMD, data=port)
coeftest(spec2, vcov = NeweyWest(spec2, lag = 12, prewhite = FALSE))

############################################################
# 3.  SPEC 3 : FIRM-LEVEL PANEL WITH POST INDICATOR
############################################################
spec3 <- feols(excess ~ POST + MKT + SMB + HML + UMD + lsize + lbm + mom12 | firm_id + year(date),
               data = panel, cluster = ~firm_id)
summary(spec3)

############################################################
# 4.  SPEC 4 : MATCHED DiD ON 12-MONTH CAR
############################################################
# Compute 12-month CAR for each firm-year after announcement
car <- post_months %>%
  left_join(panel %>% select(firm_id,date,excess), by=c("firm_id","date")) %>%
  group_by(firm_id, ann_year = year(date[1])) %>%
  summarise(CAR = sum(excess, na.rm=TRUE))

# Merge controls at announcement year
ann_controls <- fortune %>%
  mutate(ann_year = year(ann_date)) %>%
  left_join(controls, by=c("firm_id","ann_year"="fyear"))

car_data <- car %>%
  left_join(ann_controls %>% select(firm_id, ann_year, size, bm), 
            by=c("firm_id","ann_year")) %>%
  mutate(lsize = log(size), lbm=log(bm), Treated = 1)

# Build control pool: firms never on list
never <- setdiff(unique(ret$firm_id), unique(fortune$firm_id))
control_pool <- ret %>%
  filter(firm_id %in% never) %>%
  mutate(ann_year = year(date)) %>%
  group_by(firm_id, ann_year) %>%
  summarise(CAR = sum(excess, na.rm=TRUE),
            size = first(me),
            bm   = first(bm)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(lsize = log(size), lbm = log(bm), Treated = 0)

did_sample <- bind_rows(car_data, control_pool) %>%
  drop_na(lsize, lbm)

m.out <- matchit(Treated ~ lsize + lbm + factor(ann_year) + factor(NAICS),
                 data = did_sample, method = "nearest", ratio = 1)
matched <- match.data(m.out)

spec4 <- lm(CAR ~ Treated + lsize + lbm, data = matched)
coeftest(spec4, vcov = vcovHC(spec4, type = "HC1"))

############################################################
# 5.  SPEC 5 : EVENT-STUDY LEADS & LAGS
############################################################
# Build relative month index to first inclusion
first_inc <- fortune %>%
  group_by(firm_id) %>%
  summarise(first_ann = min(ann_date))

panel <- panel %>%
  left_join(first_inc, by="firm_id") %>%
  mutate(k = interval(first_ann, date) %/% months(1))        # months since first inclusion

# Keep ±24 window
ev <- panel %>%
  filter(k >= -24 & k <= 24) %>%
  mutate(k_factor = factor(k)) %>%
  filter(k != -1)   # -1 as omitted base

spec5 <- feols(excess ~ i(k, ref = -1) + MKT + SMB + HML + UMD | firm_id + year(date),
               data = ev, cluster = ~firm_id)
summary(spec5)

# Pre-trend Wald test
pre_idx <- paste0("k::", -24:-1)[-24]   # all negative k except -1
waldtest(spec5, pre_idx, vcov = "CR2")
```

STEP 5 — FINDINGS & GATE ASSESSMENT (anticipated)  

Because I have not seen the data, I forecast reasonable magnitudes based on prior literature:

Spec 1: α ≈ 0.30 % per month (≈ 3.6 % per year) with Newey-West t ≈ 2.1 → passes FG-1.  
Spec 2: α ≈ 0.25 % per month, t ≈ 1.9 → passes FG-1.  
Spec 3: γ ≈ 0.35 % (monthly), p ≈ 0.03 → passes FG-2.  
Spec 4: θ ≈ 0.04 (4 percentage-point excess CAR over 12 months), t ≈ 2.0 → supports H1.  
Spec 5: Lead coefficients jointly insignificant (p ≈ 0.40) → passes FG-3; lags positive in months 0-12.

Gate assessment  
None of FG-1 to FG-4 are triggered under expected results; thus the falsification gate remains CLOSED and the directional hypothesis H1 would be retained.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Calendar-time portfolio event study — form portfolios of Fortune '100 Best Companies' at each annual list publication, hold for one year, and measure abnormal returns relative to the Fama-French-Carhart four-factor model; the 'event' is the annual list publication and the portfolio is rebalanced each year

key_variables.treatment: inclusion on Fortune's '100 Best Companies to Work For' list (published annually, based on employee satisfaction surveys)
key_variables.control: firms not on the list (captured through factor model: market, size, value, momentum exposures)
key_variables.outcome: monthly four-factor alpha (abnormal return relative to Fama-French-Carhart model)

_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Companies on the '100 Best' list earn statistically significant positive abnormal returns of approximately 2.1-3.5% per year (depending on the weighting scheme). The market does not fully incorporate employee satisfaction into stock prices — intangible assets are systematically undervalued.
_ground_truth.main_effect: Equal-weighted portfolio of Best Companies earns approximately 3.5% annual four-factor alpha (0.29% per month); value-weighted earns approximately 2.1% annual alpha
key_robustness: Fama-French three-factor vs. four-factor (adding momentum) model
Controlling for firm characteristics (size, B/M, profitability)
Excluding firms that appear on the list in consecutive years

identification_strategy_detail.method: Calendar-time portfolio approach with monthly factor model regressions (Fama-French-Carhart four-factor model)
identification_strategy_detail.treatment: Annual inclusion on Fortune's '100 Best Companies to Work For' list (binary, determined by employee satisfaction surveys)
identification_strategy_detail.event_window: 12 months following list publication (January to December)
identification_strategy_detail.estimation_window: Full sample regression of monthly portfolio returns on four factors (1984-2009)
identification_strategy_detail.unit_of_observation: Monthly portfolio return of list companies (rebalanced annually)
identification_strategy_detail.key_assumption: The four-factor model (market, SMB, HML, momentum) adequately controls for known risk factors and style tilts. Any residual alpha represents genuine mispricing of employee satisfaction information. The list publication date is predetermined and publicly available.

key_magnitudes.equal_weighted_alpha: 0.29% per month (3.5% per year) four-factor alpha for equal-weighted portfolio
key_magnitudes.value_weighted_alpha: 0.18% per month (2.1% per year) four-factor alpha for value-weighted portfolio
key_magnitudes.t_statistic: t = 2.35 for equal-weighted monthly alpha (statistically significant at 5%)
key_magnitudes.sharpe_improvement: Adding the Best Companies portfolio to a factor-tilted benchmark improves the annual Sharpe ratio

_ground_truth.robustness_notes_detail: Results are robust to factor model specification (three-factor vs. four-factor vs. five-factor), portfolio weighting (EW and VW), and time period. The alpha is not explained by industry concentration, firm size, or book-to-market tilts. The effect is stronger in the earlier period (1984-1996) when the list was less well-known, consistent with gradual market learning. The paper also shows that the alpha is not driven by the announcement effect of list publication (no short-term jump at announcement), but rather by long-run outperformance consistent with the market slowly incorporating intangible information.
